explanation: Fires only on a '0' digit token inside a long run of zeros (e.g. '0000000[[0]]0005'); essentially silent on everything else, including other repeated characters.

Fires on color words (brown, red, white, gray, yellow, black, purple, pink-red), strongest for adjectival colors describing a noun (dark brown, brown eyes, red flesh), including capitalized Brown as a name; weaker on color words in technical/CSS contexts and weak spillover onto body-part/food nouns.
Fires only on a '0' digit token inside a long run of zeros (e.g. '0000000000[[0]]5313'); near-zero elsewhere, with tiny activations on other repeated-digit strings.

Fires on the second or later subword of a technical/domain-specific term or name being completed (mongoose, dengue, hemophilia, wasm_bindgen, dataclass, second derivative, sublicense, Initial Developer, RN), mixing code library names, biomedical terms and license boilerplate; no single semantic theme beyond 'completing a specialized term'.

Fires on tokens inside technical/specialized compound terms, often a medical/biochemical word fragment (hypothalamic, polycystic, thrombocytopenia, gallstone, root planing, sentinel node) or a code identifier/keyword (CommandType, layout_width, $schema, fill-rule); broad mixture of jargon completions across medicine, law, and code.

Fires on the start or early subword of words/names split into fragments, especially ' hydro' as a prefix (hydrophobic, hydrolysis, hydrocarbon), 'mort' (Mortimer, Morty, mortos), and syllables of proper names (Hokkaido's 'k', Kirtley, Hertsgaard, Hiroshima); moderate on assorted code/name tokens.

Mixture: fires strongly on tokens in DeepMind-style math word problems ('Let', the minus sign after 'Suppose'), on negation/modal tokens ('n't', 'not', 'can', 'possible'), and on certain CJK characters; no unifying theme.

Fires on tokens inside product version/model numbers, especially the decimal point in versions (Galaxy Tab 7[[.]]0, 5.5-inch, Studio 2.3.3) and the middle digit of years like 2010; also weaker on abbreviations/names in legal or product listings (Att'ys, Z10, Madd-ow).
Fires on a broad range of mid-phrase function or connective tokens (of, as, a, &&, =>, =") and continuation tokens in code paths and prose; no clear shared semantics.

Fires on the first fragment of a rare name or technical word split into subwords, especially proper-name surnames (Co-en, Co-aker, Co-chrane, Deg-enaar, Noor-eyezdan) and chemistry/drug terms (tet-raethylammonium, Hy-aluronic, nucle-otides), plus some list commas in drug lists; general 'start of an unusual multi-token word'.

Fires on mid-word fragments of words tokenized into odd pieces, often in non-English text (Portuguese, French, German, Japanese/Hindi byte fragments) or rare words (anticonvulsant, unspecific, endotracheal); a broad 'inside a badly tokenized word' detector.

Fires on the first token of a multi-token word or name, often a single letter or short fragment, especially in non-English (Portuguese, Spanish, Norwegian) or proper names (Gianluigi, Beira-Mar, barks, mauling); a general 'word-start fragment whose continuation is predictable' unit.

Fires mainly on tokens in authentication/security/credential contexts in code and config (SHA256, ca.pass.key, client_id, PASSWORD, password=, trust_cert, AssumeRole, private key), with weaker offshoots on chemistry word completions (polychlorinated) and privacy text.

Mixture: fires on the space token before a number in count breakdowns ('470 girls,[[ ]]450 boys'), on 'much' in 'much like / much less / much to the delight', and on words in license boilerplate ('except', 'WITHOUT', 'The'); no single theme.
